description: Fig. 14 is a single 3D stacked-bar chart (no sub-panels). The vertical axis is labelled "Cation fraction (at.%)" and is graded 0–100 with printed gridline labels 0, 20, 40, 60, 80 and 100. One horizontal axis separates the metallic elements Al, Fe and Mn, the other the four low-density-steel conditions S0, S950, S1050 and S1150, giving four bars per element row. A six-entry colour legend assigns the species: Al3+ (salmon), Fe2+ (light green), Fe3+Ox (blue), Fe3+hy (purple), Mn4+ (orange) and Mn2+ (grey). The Al bars are single salmon columns (Al3+ only) and dominate the plot: the S950 bar is the tallest, touching the 90 at.% gridline, the S1050 and S1150 bars lie just below 80 and just above 70 at.%, and the S0 bar is about half the height of S950, near the 50 at.% level. Fe bars are short stacked green-blue-purple columns whose totals stay well below the 40 at.% line, and Mn bars are the smallest, orange-over-grey stacks no higher than roughly 10 at.%. No numeric labels are printed on any bar; values can only be read against the gridlines. The chart demonstrates that the oxide films of all conditions are Al-rich, with maximum Al enrichment at S950.

observations.observation: The y-axis of the chart is labelled "Cation fraction (at.%)" and is graded 0 to 100 with printed labels 0, 20, 40, 60, 80 and 100.
The two categorical axes carry the element names Al, Fe and Mn and the sample labels S0, S950, S1050 and S1150, so each element row contains four bars.
The legend lists six species-colour pairs exactly as: Al3+ (salmon), Fe2+ (light green), Fe3+Ox (blue), Fe3+hy (purple), Mn4+ (orange), Mn2+ (grey).
All Al bars are single-coloured salmon columns (Al3+ only) and are visually the tallest bars in the chart.
The tallest Al bar reaches the 90 at.% gridline at the S950 position, whereas the S0 Al bar is only about half that height, near the 50 at.% level.
Fe bars are stacked columns combining Fe2+ (green, base), Fe3+Ox (blue, middle) and Fe3+hy (purple, top), with total heights well below the 40 at.% gridline.
Mn bars are the shortest columns, composed of Mn4+ (orange) and Mn2+ (grey), with none exceeding roughly the 10 at.% level.
No numeric data labels are printed on any of the bars; individual bar values can only be estimated against the 20 at.% gridlines.
Fig. 14 presents the relative content of different valence states of metal elements in the oxide film of the LDSs.
The relative contents of the different valence states in the oxide films of all samples were calculated using Eq. (7) from peak areas and XPS sensitivity factors.
Al is described as the predominant metallic element in the oxide films of all samples, and the S950 sample has the highest Al content in the oxide film at 90.17 at%.

The S0 sample (without solution treatment) is stated to contain substantially higher Fe and Mn contents alongside a reduced Al content, and the Al content decreases with grain coarsening accompanied by increases in Fe and Mn.
The Al content of solution-treated samples is stated still to be higher than that of the S0 sample, and grain refinement is inferred to promote preferential dissolution and film formation of Al.
The low Al content of S0 is attributed in the text to retained κ-carbide limiting the solid solubility of Al in that sample.

measured_quantities: cation fraction (at.%) of Al3+ in the oxide film
unreadable_items: Individual bar heights are not labelled; exact at.% values for each sample/element/species cannot be read and are estimated only against the 20 at.% y-axis gridlines

The 3D perspective overlap makes it ambiguous which Fe and Mn stacked bars correspond to which of S0/S950/S1050/S1150, so the caption claim that S0 has the highest Fe and Mn cannot be confirmed or refuted from the pixels alone
Fine sub-divisions of the stacked Fe bars (Fe3+Ox vs Fe3+hy boundaries) are not resolvable numerically
